v0053.A: Build a definition from the constructor that takes the data already at hand rather than through an intermediate isomorphism, and do not keep both.
v0053.B: Build a universal-property object directly from the data its constructor takes (a family of equivalences) rather than via an intermediate isomorphism, and drop the intermediate if nothing else uses it.

v0297.A: A relation that only serves as the `≤` instance is inlined into the instance, not given its own structure.
v0297.B: A predicate introduced only to state a single instance or definition should be inlined there rather than given its own named structure.

v0384.A: Statements should elaborate without explicit `@` application.
v0384.B: Lemma statements should not use `@` explicit-argument syntax; find a phrasing in which the implicit and instance arguments elaborate on their own.

v0540.A: A constructor with many fields takes a structure of its data, so users get a skeleton from code actions.
v0540.B: A constructor taking many data fields and hypotheses should take a single structure bundling them, so users can build the argument with structure-skeleton code actions.

v0587.A: A Decidable instance should evaluate efficiently, not re-evaluate the predicate quadratically.
v0587.B: A `Decidable` instance should evaluate its predicate and equality tests as few times as needed (linearly, by recursion on the list) rather than quadratically via a reformulated existential.

v0622.A: State results in simp-normal form (`1`, not `exp 0`).
v0622.B: The right-hand side of a simp lemma must be in simp-normal form: write `1`, not `exp 0`.

v0802.A: Prefer a characterisation of `range (map f g)` over a specialised monotonicity consequence.
v0802.B: Prefer a lemma characterising the object (`range (map f g) = ...`) over a specialised consequence of it; the consequence should follow from the characterisation rather than be proved on its own.

v0830.A: Long proofs are split, with the interesting estimates as their own lemmas.
v0830.B: A long proof should be split into lemmas, extracting each independently interesting estimate as its own statement.

v0891.A: State a result as an iff when the converse holds.
v0891.B: When an implication holds in both directions, state and prove it as an `iff`.

v0919.A: Factor a reusable step into a general dot-notation lemma.
v0919.B: A general fact used as a step inside a proof (a minimiser gives a lower bound) should be its own lemma, so the proof reduces to applying it.

v1112.A: Separate a construction from its application: define the general operation on generators and derive the special case.
v1112.B: A construction should be stated at the generality of what it uses: a step that does not depend on the differential module should be a standalone construction on generators, without that hypothesis.

v1149.A: Prefer a direct computation over a bounded search when one exists.
v1149.B: A decidability instance should compute its witness directly (solve the equation) rather than search a bounded window.

v1173.A: Provide the basic API (`const`, `congr`) from which specialised lemmas follow, and reserve the canonical names for the basic ones.
v1173.B: Develop the general API (`_const`, `_congr` lemmas) and derive a specialised statement from it rather than proving the specialised statement directly; reserve the `_const` name for the genuinely constant case.

v1174.A: Develop general API rather than a specialised lemma.
v1174.B: Prefer general API to a specialised lemma; a specialised statement should come with, or be replaced by, the general lemmas it follows from.

v1191.A: State results as characterisations independent of a particular instance construction.
v1191.B: State a fact as a characterisation (`boundedSpace_iff_edist`) in terms of existing structure rather than as a lemma whose statement builds a particular instance with `letI`.

v1267.A: Do not quantify over a universe of index types inside a class; then extensionality is a theorem, not a field.
v1267.B: A structure field that is provable from the other fields (here by `funext`) should be a theorem, not a field.

v1456.A: Formalise the recurring mathematical concept (adjacent sequences) rather than the ad hoc instance.
v1456.B: Name the general mathematical notion underlying the argument (adjacent sequences: one increasing, one decreasing, same limit) and prove the result through it rather than inline.

v1457.A: Define the object you will reason about (the iterated sequence) directly, not only one step.
v1457.B: Define the object actually studied (the sequence of iterates, or the pair of sequences) rather than only its one-step generator, so lemmas are stated about the sequence directly.

v1459.A: A definition made with `choose` comes with lemmas exposing its `choose_spec` properties.
v1459.B: A definition made by `Classical.choose` should come with lemmas exposing its defining property (`choose_spec`), so users never unfold the choice.

v1497.A: State the strongest natural consequence (an isomorphism) rather than partial facts.
v1497.B: When a stronger structural fact (an isomorphism of the residue field with the reals) holds under the same hypotheses, establish it and derive the piecemeal lemmas from it.

v1549.A: State lemmas with expanded functions rather than compositions.
v1549.B: In statements, write an explicit lambda rather than a chain of function compositions; it is more readable and easier to rewrite.

v1592.A: Introduce a definition at its most general level, with API, or leave a TODO.
v1592.B: A `Finset` operation built from a `List` operation should pass through a `Multiset` version, following the List -> Multiset -> Finset layering, and each layer needs its own API (or a TODO).

v1645.A: Provide the universe-polymorphic `OfSize` form of a preservation instance.
v1645.B: Provide the most general instance available (`PreservesLimitsOfSize`) rather than the per-shape one, since the general instance yields the specific ones.

v1907.A: Express a property of objects as an `ObjectProperty` and state conditions with `IsIso`, not bespoke structures.
v1907.B: State a property of objects with the library's standard predicates (`IsIso`) and package the subcategory with `ObjectProperty`/`FullSubcategory` (or a typeclass) rather than a bespoke structure.

v1992.A: Extract an inline construction into an auxiliary definition.
v1992.B: A large term built inline inside a proof (`letI G : Grp C := {...}`) should be a named auxiliary definition, so it can be stated, reused and its proof obligations tidied separately.

v1998.A: Define the general functorial object (iteration as a functor) instead of ad hoc recursive definitions.
v1998.B: Define the general construction (the iterates of an endofunctor as a functor `ℕ ⥤ C ⥤ C`) and obtain the special case (iterates applied at the initial object) from it.

v2037.A: When a structure extends another, define the extended one directly rather than in two stages.
v2037.B: When the target structure extends an intermediate one, define the target directly rather than building the intermediate first and upgrading it.

v2066.A: A fact used inside a proof is its own lemma.
v2066.B: An independently meaningful fact proved inline inside a case of a proof (`Φ 0 = 0`) should be its own lemma.

v2112.A: Give a default instance by its canonical construction, not through a general helper.
v2112.B: Construct a canonical element (the empty partition) directly rather than through a roundabout construction, so its definitional unfolding is the obvious one.

v2117.A: State a result as an iff when the converse holds.
v2117.B: When an implication holds in both directions, state it as an `iff`.

v2263.A: Generalise the core of a proof to a lemma about the underlying general construction.
v2263.B: Prove the general statement (about `gfpApprox f x` when `f x = x`) as a lemma and derive the specific instance from it.
